text: Welcome back. Today we cover concurrency problems in operating systems, starting with race conditions.
A race condition happens when two threads read and write shared data and the result depends on timing.
We fix races with locks. A mutex lets only one thread into the critical section at a time.
But locks create a new problem: deadlock. Two threads each hold one lock and wait forever for the other.
Deadlock needs four conditions: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait.
To prevent deadlock, break one condition. The usual trick is a global lock ordering, which removes circular wait.
Semaphores generalize locks with a counter. They are useful for producer and consumer queues.
Next week: scheduling. Read chapter seven before then.
